a:r.a:t: Large 50S subunit combines with the 30S subunit forming the

p:cNvPr.descr: A complex diagram shows the steps in formation of an initiation complex. The diagram begins at the top with the 30S subunit. It is a large cup-shaped subunit, which has three binding sites, E, P, and A. They are shaded a darker orange to indicate that they are set into the subunit. Above the 30S subunit are two blue ovals, which are the initiation factors IF3 (left) and IF1 (right). Arrows curve down to show that they are being bonded to the sites on the 30S. Below this image is an arrow pointing down. It has a convergent arrow on the right showing addition of mRNA. To the right is (1), then a gray text box reading, "The 30S subunit binds IF1 and IF3, then the mRNA." The arrow points down to the next step. Here, the IF1 has bound to the A site, and the IF3 is in the process of binding to the E site. A strand of mRNA curves along the bottoms of the E, P, and A sites and continues to the right. The sequence, which begins on the left at its 5' end, has a short green sequence at the very end. Then, there is a longer orange sequence labeled "Shine-Dalgarno sequence" to the left. To the right of it is another short green sequence, then a longer dark green sequence labeled "AUG." To the right of the AUG sequence is a yellow sequence, after which is a long green sequence which slopes downward off the 30S subunit and continues to the right in a straight line. Below the Shine-Dalgarno sequence, there is a short cadet blue segment labeled "16S rRNA." Below this image is an arrow pointing down. On the left there are two convergent arrows. The first arrow shows input of IF2 bonded on the left to GTP. The IF2 is represented by a blue sphere. The second arrow shows input of an anticodon attached to a tRNA molecule. The tRNA is a twisted green tube with the yellow shaded anticodon at the bottom (3' to 5'). The tRNA's amino acid arm, at the top, is attached to fMet, which is represented by a light blue sphere. On the right is (2), then a gray text box which reads, "IF2-GTP binds the 30S subunit and recruits fMet-tRNSAfMet, which base-pairs with the start codon." The arrow points down to another image of the 30S subunit with the mRNA still running across its front, underneath the binding sites. IF3, on the left, is attached to the E site, but is not fully settled in it. The fMet-tRNAfMet binds to the P site. The IF2-GTP binds to the top of the IF1 at the A site. Below this image is a long arrow pointing down. It has a convergent arrow on the left showing addition of the 50S subunit, and a divergent arrow on the right showing removal of GDP + Pi. On the right, below the first divergent arrow, is another divergent arrow showing removal of the IF1, IF2, and IF3. Below this is (3), then a gray text box that reads, "The 50S subunit associates, IF2 hydrolyzes GTP, and IF1, IF2, and IF3 dissociates, leaving the 70S initiation complex. The arrow points down to a final image. Here, the 30S subunit no longer has the initiation factors attached to its E and A sites. The tRNA is still in the P site, and the mRNA strand is still on the 30S. The yellow sequence on it is labeled "next codon"; the blue 16S rRNA fragment has also been removed. A very large yellow subunit, shaped like the cap of a mushroom and labeled "50S subunit" has attached to the top of the 30S subunit. It is round on top and has E, P, and A sites as well, which align with those on the 30S subunit. The tRNA with the anticodon extends up into the P site of the 50S subunit. This whole structure is labeled "70S initiation complex" on the right.
